purpose: Independent practice of C2.1 (variables as placeholders).
student_learning_goal: I can recognise when a symbol stands for an unknown number.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can recognise when a symbol stands for an unknown number.
header.character_watermark: Detective Dee in the top-right corner. Small (~1.5in tall).

parts.student_instructions: Circle the variable in each equation. The variable is the symbol that stands for an unknown.
parts.visual_layout: Top of page. Six equation rows.

image_placeholders.description: Six equation rows in B&W line-art, ~7in x 3in. Pre-printed equations: 5 + ? = 12, n - 4 = 6, ☐ + 7 = 15, 20 = m + 5, 14 - ___ = 8, x + 9 = 18. Header 'Circle the Variable:'.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P1_FIND: keywords (variable, circle) name what the rows ask for.

parts.answer_key: Each variable should be circled: ?, n, ☐, m, ___, x.

parts.part_title: Part 2: What Does It Stand For?
parts.student_instructions: Match each equation to the unknown number it stands for.
parts.visual_layout: Middle of page. Four equations on the left, four numbers on the right.

image_placeholders.description: Four matching pairs in B&W line-art, ~7in x 2.5in. Left column: 5 + ? = 12, n - 3 = 4, ☐ + 6 = 14, 10 = m + 2. Right column: 7, 8, 8, 7. Header 'Match the Variable to its Value:'.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P2_MATCH: keywords (match, value) name what the pairs ask for.

parts.student_instructions: Write 3 of your own equations using a variable. Pick any symbol — box, blank, or letter.
parts.visual_layout: Bottom of page. Three numbered equation slots.

image_placeholders.description: Three numbered equation slots in B&W line-art, ~7in x 2.5in. Each slot has '1.', '2.', '3.' on the left with a long equation line. Header 'My Equations with a Variable:'.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P3_OWN: keywords (my, equations) name what the slots ask for.

parts.answer_key: Open. Each equation must include a variable symbol.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, swap with a partner and identify each other's variables.
teacher_notes: Lesson 1 worksheet introduces C2.1 (variables). Watch for the variable-as-answer confusion — children who write 'box = 7' instead of 'box stands for 7'. Part 2: rewritten so children MATCH each equation to a description of the unknown ('the number that with 5 makes 12') without computing the value. Solving comes Lesson 2; today's job is to NAME the variable.
